DESCRIPTION
Del-Mar-Va Heartland magazine, summer 1977. Feature article on steamboats, including pictures of the Joppa. Also Bird watching article (pp18-20), Recipes and local real estate ads.

The Joppa is mentioned on p. 8, pictured on p.9 -- Built in 1885 for the Maryland Steamboat Company. Served the Choptank River until the early 1920s. known as one of the faster boats.

Governor Emerson C. Harrington is pictured on p. 7 at the Claiborne dock. A side-wheel steamer converted to carry automobiles began the Annapolis-Claiborne run in 1919. Automobiles were loaded from the side and after some twisting and backing were stowed forward.

The Talbot is picture on p.8 -- added to the fleet in 1912 for the Potomac River. Considered queen of the fleet. length of 192' with a 60' beam. Ran aground on the Tred Avon River.

Emma Giles is pictured at Lowe's Wharf on p.6. Built in 1887 for the Tochester Steamboat Company. It serviced the Little Choptank and Miles River.
